solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One cleans up, making a tidy pile

definitions.text: One cleans up, making a tidy pile

blocks.note: surface reading: someone tidying a room, heaping the mess into a neat stack
setter's reading: the pile is the raised nap of a carpet, left neat after a household appliance has been pushed over it

explanation.walkthrough: A 'tidy pile' suggests a heap of collected rubbish, but pile here is the soft surface of a carpet, which the machine sucks clean and leaves standing neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The household appliance sucks dust from carpets, so it literally cleans up and leaves the carpet nap neat.

clue.text: Having run out of polish, Grecian ordered male cosmetic

indicators.note: when you are out of something you no longer have it, so a letter goes missing from the word
to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are rearranged into a new sequence

blocks.note: varnish is a glossy polish
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man's Grecian hair product, ordered in after the shoe polish ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: VARNISH loses its R to give VANISH; GRECIAN plus M is then rearranged to finish the phrase. Grecian 2000 is a men's hair dye, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a light skin moisturiser that seems to disappear when rubbed in, a beauty product of the cosmetic kind.

clue.text: Quibble about very vacuous individual

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its insides and only its outer letters remain

blocks.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
V is the usual abbreviation for very
only the first and last letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Someone raises a petty objection about a very empty-headed person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very vacuous' reads as one phrase describing the individual, but very gives V on its own and vacuous works only on individual.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise trivial objections, a close synonym for nitpicking or petty fault-finding.

clue.text: Dramatic Russian acts – prepare clean navy uniform first thing

indicators.note: to prepare something is to work it into a new form, so these letters are reorganised
the first thing comes at the very start, so this letter is placed ahead of the rest

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Before a dramatic Russian performance, sailors are told to get their navy uniforms clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sailors smartening up, but the uniform supplies only its NATO letter U, which goes in front of the reworked CLEAN NAVY.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Vanya is Chekhov's four-act play, so a piece of Russian theatre written in several acts.

clue.text: Flipping puppet Emu lackadaisically swallows peace pipe

indicators.note: what is swallowed sits inside, so the letters lie within the run of clue words
to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Emu, the puppet, lazily gulps down a peace pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Emu was the aggressive puppet bird of British TV entertainer Rod Hull; 'Flipping' sounds like a mild curse but signals the turnaround of the concealed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A calumet is the ceremonial tobacco pipe of North American Indigenous peoples, smoked to seal treaties and goodwill.

clue.text: Almost exposed party member’s top rank

indicators.note: something exposed has had its covering stripped, so the outer letters are taken off
the top of a down entry is its start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: almost is NEARLY, which loses its first and last letters
a do is a party
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A party member nearly exposed as holding top rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top rank' looks like the definition, but top belongs to the wordplay; rank alone is defined, and NEARLY stripped of its ends gives EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the dignity or title of an earl, one of the grades of the British peerage.

clue.text: Vulgar, loud supporter from the South

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom upward means the letters come out backwards

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a fan supports a team or star

explanation.surface: A crass, noisy fan from the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff describes something tasteless or lacking in style, so it overlaps with crude and common in meaning.

clue.text: Pub wake after burying Bill – oh, getting upset

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it inside, so one piece is placed within another
upset means knocked over, and in a down entry that turns letters upside down

blocks.note: to rouse someone is to wake them
an ad, an advertisement, is a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wake held in the pub after a funeral for Bill turns emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: Wake, burying and upset all suggest a funeral, but wake is just the verb to rouse, and Bill is an advertisement, not a dead man.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or tavern on a main road outside town, so a type of drinking establishment.

clue.text: Let’s hope it’s not as tough as old boots!

definitions.text: Let’s hope it’s not as tough as old boots!

blocks.clueFragment: Let’s hope it’s not as tough
blocks.note: surface reading: a hope that a meat dish served at dinner turns out tender
setter's reading: the dish shares its name with a rubber boot, so the joke is that it shouldn't be as chewy as footwear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough as old boots' is an idiom for very hardy or chewy; a wellington is a British rubber boot, and the dish is fillet steak baked in pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is a fillet steak wrapped in pastry, which a cook hopes is tender rather than leathery like rubber footwear.

clue.text: Russian chap, retired copper, left a river boat thus described

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A Russian man and a retired policeman left a riverboat, which is described here.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol; the definition is the phrase at the end, meaning shaped like a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Navicular, from Latin navicula 'little ship', means boat-shaped, the adjective used for such a form.

clue.text: Sweet piece that’s traditionally suited to cornet?

definitions.text: Sweet piece that’s traditionally suited to cornet?

blocks.clueFragment: Sweet piece that’s traditionally suited to cornet
blocks.note: surface reading: a tuneful composition written for the brass instrument
setter's reading: a cornet is also an ice-cream cone, and a classic one comes with a crumbly chocolate bar pushed into it

explanation.walkthrough: A 'sweet piece' for cornet suggests a melody, but the cornet is a cone of ice cream; in Britain a '99' is a soft ice with a Cadbury chocolate stick of this name stuck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cadbury bar of thin folded chocolate is the confection traditionally pushed into a British soft-serve ice-cream cone.

clue.text: Your challenge: catching five flatfish

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase; the answer is the imperative verb that states the challenge

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a sole is a flatfish
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An angler is challenged to land five flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition addresses the solver directly: the task set by every clue is this single command.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out the answer is exactly what a puzzle asks of its reader, so the imperative states the task given to you.

clue.text: Second daughter beginning to enjoy fashion

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A younger daughter starts to take pleasure in clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second daughter' reads as one person, but second gives MO and daughter gives D separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Mode is a prevailing style or vogue, a direct synonym taken from the French word for current style.

clue.text: One who prepares cold and hot oeufs every now and again?

definitions.text: One who prepares cold and hot oeufs every now and again?

indicators.note: doing something only now and again means at intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
the second and fourth letters of the French word

explanation.surface: A cook who serves eggs both cold and hot from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay; oeufs is French for eggs, which suits a French-named cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a kitchen, someone who makes egg dishes among many others.

clue.text: Trim the CIA – crazy sums!

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to cut the American intelligence agency's budget, given the mad amounts it spends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' reads as a demand for budget cuts, but it simply supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums are calculations with numbers, the basic activity that makes up school mathematics of this elementary kind.

clue.text: Base tax, NIC adjusted? That’s not quite right

indicators.note: adjusting something changes its arrangement, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that basic-rate tax and National Insurance have been miscalculated.
explanation.walkthrough: Base suggests the basic rate of income tax, but it is the mathematical constant e. NIC is National Insurance Contributions, a British payroll tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise or slightly off, which is what being a little wrong means.

clue.text: Warmer red that is turning blue?

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: A question about something warmer red that changes colour to blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Warmer looks like a comparative adjective about colour temperature, but it is a noun: a thing that keeps you warm.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a thick quilt filled with duck feathers, laid on a bed to keep the sleeper cosy.

clue.text: Brand new unwrapped tent

indicators.note: unwrapping removes the outer layer, so only the inside of the word survives

blocks.note: a marque is a brand, especially of car
the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A brand-new tent just taken out of its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand new' reads as one phrase meaning unused, but brand and new work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties, weddings and outdoor functions.

clue.text: Light-headed riding nag – so stimulated!

blocks.note: giddy means dizzy or light-headed
a jockey who is riding a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: A dizzy rider on an old horse, excited by the experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riding nag' looks like a phrase about a horse, but riding gives UP, and the definition is the call by which a nag is so stimulated.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy-up is the exclamation a rider uses to urge a horse to start or go faster.

clue.text: American skunk/weed Alec inhaled when cycling

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so the front letter moves to the back
what is inhaled is taken inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called weed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Alec smokes some weed while out on his bike, and the slash pairs it with a skunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Skunk and weed are both cannabis slang, which drives the surface; cycling here means moving the first letter to the end, not riding a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America polecat is a regional name for the skunk, a different animal from the European polecat.

clue.text: Old mate, terribly bald, discovered healthy breakfast food

indicators.note: done terribly means done badly and messily, so the letters are jumbled
dis-covered means with its cover removed, so the outer letters go and the inside stays

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written
the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: An old friend, shockingly bald, has found a wholesome breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovered looks like 'found', but read as dis-covered it strips the outside of the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats cooked as porridge, a nutritious morning cereal dish.

clue.text: Each November visiting boundlessly gregarious island neighbours

indicators.note: without bounds means without its edges, so the first and last letters are dropped
a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so these letters sit within another word

blocks.note: a gregarious person is social
EA is the abbreviation for each
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Every November, friendly islanders from nearby come to call.
explanation.walkthrough: Gregarious must first become its synonym before losing its edges; neighbours describes the Pacific nations as a group of islands near each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region of Pacific islands together with Australia and New Zealand, nations that lie close to one another.

clue.text: A Ferry song about boating’s intro on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard rather than seen, so we go by how words sound

blocks.note: the nursery song begins 'Row, row, row your boat'; intro means its opening words

explanation.surface: A Bryan Ferry song about boating, its opening bars heard on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital F makes Ferry the singer Bryan Ferry, but here it is a boat. The opening of 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat' gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off vessel that vehicles drive straight onto and off, a type of car-carrying boat.

clue.text: Wartime spies quaffing large gin tinged with this?

indicators.note: to quaff is to drink down, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: the Special Operations Executive ran British agents in the Second World War
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Secret agents in the war knocking back a big gin flavoured with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'gin tinged with this': the answer is the fruit that flavours a well-known liqueur gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloes are blackthorn berries steeped in spirit to make sloe gin, giving it a pinkish colour and fruity taste.

clue.text: Not seeing clearly, backward point takes over leg side position

indicators.note: going backward means facing the other way, so the letters run in reverse
one piece takes on another by having it attached, so the two go side by side

blocks.note: dim-sighted describes poor vision
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at backward point, unable to see properly, takes over another position on the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: Backward point and leg side are cricket terms, but backward is the reversal sign and point is a compass letter. Mid-on is a fielding place near the bowler on the batter's leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-on is a cricket fielding spot on the on side, which is also called the leg side.

clue.text: Belief is liberating exploit from negative mindset

indicators.note: liberating something frees it from where it was held, so these letters are taken out

blocks.note: defeatism is a pessimistic expectation of failure
a feat is a notable exploit

explanation.surface: Faith sets a person free from a pessimistic outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberating sounds like a positive property of faith, but it frees the FEAT from DEFEATISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is the religious conviction that God created the universe but does not intervene, a kind of faith.

clue.text: Execute witch around noon

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A witch is to be put to death at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a witch trial; the witch is a HAG and noon supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang someone is to put them to death by the noose, one method of carrying out a death sentence.

clue.text: Arabian sultanate exporting new perfume

indicators.note: exporting sends goods out of a country, so a letter is sent out of the word

blocks.note: Ar. is the abbreviation for Arabian or Arabic
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A Gulf sultanate sending a new scent abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabian sultanate' reads as a single description of Oman, but Arabian gives AR on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfume can mean a pleasant smell, and aroma is a distinctive, usually agreeable fragrance.

clue.text: Contract Tories reportedly swindled?

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

blocks.note: Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tory party
tricked means swindled

explanation.surface: A government contract on which the Conservatives were allegedly cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract looks like a noun for a deal, but it is the verb meaning shrink. Tories are Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to squeeze or narrow, so it means to make or become smaller and tighter.

clue.text: One sent in to defend character of Dutch master?

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, a lower-order batter sent in late in a day's play to protect the better batters
second meaning: a figure in Rembrandt's famous militia painting The Night Watch

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, when a wicket falls near the close of play a tail-end batter goes in to survive until stumps; Rembrandt's great group portrait gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketing sense is a defensive tail-end batter, and the painting shows members of a civic guard, each one a guard by night.
